analysis:
The only change to docs/architecture/inference.md is documentation: the 'Last updated' date bump and a new section, 'GPT-OSS decode command buffers' (head lines 4816-4826). The section says GPT-OSS plain decode commits a Metal command buffer every 100 operations with no input-size bound, whereas MLX defaults commit every 40-50 operations or 40-50M input elements. The stated rationale is that default commits fired after almost every MoE layer and waited on MLX's limit of ten command buffers in flight, and the document says results do not depend on the partitioning. Prefill chunks keep MLX defaults. This is a performance and scheduling description only. The two supplied units are base_text excerpts (base lines 2465-3234) of surrounding unchanged content, and the changed lines sit outside both excerpts. I examined them against the threat model for any security-relevant drift.

I saw no change to encryption, attestation, authorization, the coordinator WebSocket (TB-002), the prefix-cache posture (T-041), the add-on hold (TB-012), or key custody (A-003). The documentation does not weaken any stated mitigation or assumption, and there is no new attack surface or invalidated assumption. The underlying code change (the GPTOSSDecodeCommandBuffers implementation and the CBv2DecodeCommandBufferLimitsProviding protocol) is not in the supplied evidence. A reviewer of the source change should check that the unbounded input-size commit does not raise peak GPU memory in a way that bypasses the admission or KV budget gates (T-029 and DoS-class availability). That cannot be judged from the documentation alone, and I did not make it a finding.
